title: [ORION-QG QG-36] Exact fair fixed-vs-adaptive post-summary composition
body:
Parent programme: #740.
Prospective baseline parent: QG-35 #932 (summary-conditioned nonadaptive fixed probe complexity; outcome unknown at freeze).
Earned adaptive parent: QG-34 #924 (`D_* = 3` exact on the frozen 715-orbit / 92 joint-summary-class observation problem).
Earned universal fixed context: QG-32c #928 (universal fixed minimum 5; context only, not the fair comparator).

## Status

**PROSPECTIVE COMPOSITION RULE. FREEZE BEFORE ANY QG-35 RESULT.**

The fair comparison must give fixed and adaptive policies the same side information: the joint bulk+spectrum summary class is known before any indexed probe is selected.

QG-35 will earn, if exact, `F(S)` = minimum number of probes chosen after class `S` is known but fixed before response outcomes, and `F_* = max_S F(S)`.
QG-34 has already earned `D_* = 3` for adaptive policies under the same known-class side information.

QG-36 is a pure receipt composition. It performs no new search and must not inspect raw hidden compiler states beyond the two parent receipts.

## Frozen decision table

If either parent lacks exact authority -> `QG36_CANNOT_CHECK`.

If `D_* > F_*` -> `QG36_PARENT_INCONSISTENCY__ADAPTIVE_WORSE_THAN_OPTIMAL_FIXED` because an adaptive policy can emulate any fixed policy.

If `D_* == F_*` -> `QG36_NO_STRICT_POSTSUMMARY_ADAPTIVITY_ADVANTAGE__EXACT_TIE`.

If `D_* < F_*` -> `QG36_TARE_POSTSUMMARY_ADAPTIVITY_STRICTLY_REDUCES_WORST_CASE_OBSERVATION_COUNT`.

No value of `F_*` is predicted.

## Allowed positive interpretation

Only the strict branch may authorize:
`TARE_POSTSUMMARY_ADAPTIVITY_STRICTLY_REDUCES_WORST_CASE_OBSERVATION_COUNT=true`.

This means only: conditional choice of the next indexed structural probe reduces worst-case **observation count** for identifying the frozen 715-way indexed local-response state after the joint summary is known.

It does not imply lower compilation cost, physical quantum advantage, hardware measurement optimality, or generic active-learning novelty.

## Required composition checks

- QG-34 exact adaptive receipt bound by hash and exact scope;
- QG-35 exact class-conditioned fixed receipt bound by hash and exact scope;
- same 715 orbits / 384 probes / 92 joint classes and same class ordering/hash;
- `D(S) <= F(S)` for every one of the 92 classes, not only the maxima;
- exact maxima recomputed from the parent class-depth/minimum arrays;
- false-authority fields remain false.

## Verification

Production composition: read only immutable QG-34/QG-35 committed receipts and apply the frozen decision table.
Generic ORION: independently recompute all 92 pointwise inequalities and maxima from the receipts.
Native ORION-Q: authorize only the observation-count comparison.
Workflow: deterministic replay + self-consistent parent-array/max tamper rejection.

## Hard boundaries

Always false:
- compiler optimization-cost advantage;
- hardware/measurement minimum;
- full finite-n identification optimum;
- generic adaptive-testing novelty;
- autonomous skill-selection authority;
- physical quantum advantage.

nodes.body: **Retraction notice (now on main via #926).** The headline this issue builds on is null-reproducible: the separation counts (`85/92`, `708/715`, `D_*=3 < F_*=4 < U_*=5`, the regret curve) are reproduced by a row-shuffle null, and `85 = 92−7` / `708 = 715−7` are identities forced by the class-size histogram frozen before any solver ran. See `development/orion-qg-regime-geometry/QG_RETRACTION_SELECTION_HEADLINES_V1.md` and `QG_ADVERSARIAL_REFEREE_REPORT.md`. What survives: C1(b) descriptor completeness (whose ceiling theorem is Lehmann 1959 per the lane's own prior-art audit), witness disjointness, and the depth-3 residual (16 classes / 168 masks vs null-A mean 8.9 / 384 — noting null B in the residual script is uninformative by construction, being exactly permutation-invariant). Work on this issue should either retarget the surviving residual or close as superseded.
